san_ichneumon.name: outwits and corrects his grandfather the Mantis
san_ichneumon.notes: In the Bleek-Lloyd /Xam cycle the Ichneumon (mongoose) is the sharp, knowing young one who repeatedly sees through /Kaggen's foolish schemes, scolds him and sets him right, carried in his grandfather's bag yet wiser than him.

sources.reference: W. H. I. Bleek & L. C. Lloyd, Specimens of Bushman Folklore (1911)

san_young_kwammanga.name: carries the rainbow-being's nature as the elder son named after his father
san_young_kwammanga.notes: Eldest son of the rainbow-being /Kwammang-a and the Porcupine; bears his father's name and the rainbow descent within the Mantis's mythic household.

sources.reference: W. H. I. Bleek & L. C. Lloyd, Specimens of Bushman Folklore (1911)

santal_marang_buru.name: is invoked as the great mountain, cause of all causes
santal_marang_buru.notes: As the 'Great Mountain,' Marang Buru is propitiated first at every festival and major undertaking and reckoned the cause of all causes, securing rain, fertility and protection.

sources.reference: P. O. Bodding, Studies in Santal Medicine and Connected Folklore (1925-1940)

santal_thakur_jiu.name: breathes the life-force (jiu) into the first human pair
santal_thakur_jiu.notes: After fashioning humans the supreme being Thakur Jiu breathes into them the jiu, the divine life-breath; his name itself joins thakur 'lord' with jiu 'life/spirit'.

sources.reference: P. O. Bodding, Traditions and Institutions of the Santals (Horkoren Mare Hapramko Reak Katha, 1942)

scythian_tabiti.name: sends sickness on the king when a false oath is sworn by her hearth
scythian_tabiti.notes: Herodotos 4.68: when the Scythian king fell ill the diviners declared that someone had sworn falsely by the royal hearth-fires (Tabiti); the oath-breaker's death restored the king.

sources.reference: Herodotus, Histories 4.68

scythian_tabiti.name: is named queen of the Scythians, head of the gods
scythian_tabiti.notes: Idanthyrsos invokes 'Zeus my ancestor and Hestia queen of the Scythians' (Herodotos 4.127), the formula by which Tabiti stands at the head of the heptad as supreme deity.

sources.reference: Herodotus, Histories 4.127

scythian_argimpasa.name: strikes her offending diviners with the 'female sickness'
scythian_argimpasa.notes: Herodotos (1.105, 4.67) reports that the Aphrodite-Ourania of Ascalon/Scythia afflicted a lineage with the thelea nousos ('female sickness'); these Enarees became her androgynous diviners.

sources.reference: Herodotus, Histories 1.105; 4.67

scythian_argimpasa.name: grants prophecy to the Enarees who divine by lime-tree bark
scythian_argimpasa.notes: Her Enaree priests received the gift of divination; Herodotos 4.67 notes they prophesy by splitting strips of lime-bark, twisting and untwisting them about their fingers.

sources.reference: Herodotus, Histories 4.67

scythian_snake_legged_goddess.name: declares herself mistress of the land and keeps Heracles' mares
scythian_snake_legged_goddess.notes: In Herodotos 4.9 the half-woman, half-serpent being holds the strayed mares of Heracles, telling him she is the mistress of the country and will return them only if he lies with her.

sources.reference: Herodotus, Histories 4.9

selknam_temaukel.name: sends the culture-hero Kenos to order the unfinished world
selknam_temaukel.notes: The supreme being dwells beyond the stars and does not act directly; he dispatches Kenos to mould the first ancestors and shape the land, then withdraws to uphold the moral order.

sources.reference: Martin Gusinde, Die Feuerland-Indianer, Band I: Die Selk'nam (1931)

selknam_shoort.name: erupts from the ground to terrorise the women and test initiates
selknam_shoort.notes: In the Hain, Shoort (impersonated by painted, masked men) breaks out of the earth to attack the women's huts and frighten the candidates, serving his wife Xalpen's appetites.

sources.reference: Anne Chapman, Drama and Power in a Hunting Society: The Selk'nam of Tierra del Fuego (1982)

selknam_xalpen.name: devours the Hain initiates underground and then restores them to life
selknam_xalpen.notes: The huge subterranean Xalpen is said to seize and consume the young men inside the Hain lodge and afterward give them back alive; unlike the other spirits she is never embodied but represented offstage.

sources.reference: Anne Chapman, Drama and Power in a Hunting Society: The Selk'nam of Tierra del Fuego (1982)

selkup_nom.name: personifies the sky and dispenses weather, game and food
selkup_nom.notes: Nom (cognate with Samoyed Num) is the high celestial deity who is the sky itself, sending weather and granting the people their food and game.

sources.reference: Natalya A. Tuchkova et al., Selkup Mythology (Encyclopaedia of Uralic Mythologies 4, 2010)

sources.reference: J. M. Orpen, 'A Glimpse into the Mythology of the Maluti Bushmen,' Cape Monthly Magazine (1874)

sources.reference: Herodotus, Histories 4.59

scythian_goitosyros.gloss: Apollo (Herodotos' interpretatio for the Scythian sun-god)

sources.reference: Herodotus, Histories 4.59

san_gauwa.name: The healing trance-dance (curing dance)
san_gauwa.cadence: as needed for the sick, and at communal night dances
san_gauwa.notes: To fight //Gauwa and the //gauwasi (spirits of the dead) who shoot invisible arrows of sickness, the n/um-possessing healers dance into trance, lay hands on the sick, draw the arrows into themselves and expel them with trembling and cries; the curing dance and the power n/um are themselves said to derive from //Gauwa.

sources.reference: Lorna Marshall, Nyae Nyae !Kung Beliefs and Rites (1999)

santal_marang_buru.name: Sacrifice of white fowl or white goat with rice-beer
santal_marang_buru.cadence: at every festival and major rite
santal_marang_buru.notes: Marang Buru is propitiated first at all Santal festivals through the sacrifice of a white fowl or white goat, accompanied by libations of rice-beer (handi); his invocation requires the first offering of the brew.

sources.reference: P. O. Bodding, Studies in Santal Medicine and Connected Folklore (1925-1940)

santal_jaher_era.name: Worship in the village sacred grove (Jaher)
santal_jaher_era.notes: Jaher Era, the lady of the grove, is worshipped with the other grove-spirits at the village Jaher (a stand of preserved sal trees on the village edge) during the annual festival cycle (notably Baha and Sohrae), where fowl are sacrificed for communal welfare, rain and protection from epidemics.

sources.reference: P. O. Bodding, Traditions and Institutions of the Santals (Horkoren Mare Hapramko Reak Katha, 1942)

sarmatian_sword_god.name: Worship of a sword planted in the earth
sarmatian_sword_god.notes: Ammianus Marcellinus 31.2.23 reports that the Alani fix a bared sword point-down in the ground and reverence it as their god of war and presiding deity of the lands they range, a survival of the Scythian sword-cult of Ares.

sources.reference: Ammianus Marcellinus, Res Gestae 31.2.23

scythian_tabiti.name: Oath and sacrifice at the royal hearth-fire
scythian_tabiti.cadence: the binding royal oath; sickness-rites of the king
scythian_tabiti.notes: The most solemn Scythian oath was sworn by the royal hearth-fires (Tabiti); to swear falsely by them was believed to sicken the king and was punished with death (Herodotos 4.68). As the steppe Hestia she received the first portion of every sacrifice.

sources.reference: Herodotus, Histories 4.68

scythian_argimpasa.name: Divination by the androgynous Enarees
scythian_argimpasa.cadence: on demand, by her hereditary diviners
scythian_argimpasa.notes: Her hereditary Enaree diviners, struck with the 'female sickness,' served as her androgynous priests and prophesied by splitting and twisting strips of lime-tree bark about their fingers (Herodotos 4.67).

sources.reference: Herodotus, Histories 4.67

scythian_thagimasadas.name: Cult of the Royal Scythians (Paralatae) alone
scythian_thagimasadas.notes: Herodotos 4.59 specifies that, whereas the other gods were worshipped by all Scythians, the Royal Scythians alone sacrificed to Thagimasadas, the patron equated with Poseidon and associated with water and horses.

sources.reference: Herodotus, Histories 4.59

selkup_nom.name: Bloody and bloodless sacrifice to the sky
selkup_nom.notes: Sacrifices to Nom/Num are either bloody (the killing of a reindeer or dog) or bloodless (offerings of food, cloth and money), made at appointed times to the high god of the sky.

sources.reference: Natalya A. Tuchkova et al., Selkup Mythology (Encyclopaedia of Uralic Mythologies 4, 2010)

attributes.name: the shoe cast into the sky as the moon
attributes.notes: Frustrated by walking in the dark, the Mantis throws his (or an antelope's) shoe/leather into the sky, where it becomes the moon, glowing red because it is still leather.

sources.reference: W. H. I. Bleek & L. C. Lloyd, Specimens of Bushman Folklore (1911)

sacredAnimals.name: praying mantis
sacredAnimals.notes: His most characteristic theriomorphic form, from which the /Xam name itself derives.

sources.reference: W. H. I. Bleek & L. C. Lloyd, Specimens of Bushman Folklore (1911)

sacredAnimals.name: eland
sacredAnimals.notes: The bull eland is his beloved first creation and another shape he assumes; the eland is the central sacred animal of San cosmology and rock art.

sources.reference: J. M. Orpen, 'A Glimpse into the Mythology of the Maluti Bushmen,' Cape Monthly Magazine (1874)

attributes.name: the colours of the rainbow in the sky
attributes.notes: The First-Race being /Kwammang-a is the rainbow itself, neither wholly human nor animal, manifesting as the bands of colour in the sky.

sources.reference: W. H. I. Bleek & L. C. Lloyd, Specimens of Bushman Folklore (1911)

sacredAnimals.name: ichneumon (Egyptian mongoose)
sacredAnimals.notes: The being is the mongoose itself, grandson of the Mantis through the Porcupine and the rainbow-being.

sources.reference: W. H. I. Bleek & L. C. Lloyd, Specimens of Bushman Folklore (1911)

sacredAnimals.name: porcupine
sacredAnimals.notes: The First-Race being !Xo is the Porcupine, adopted daughter of the Mantis and wife of the rainbow-being /Kwammang-a.

sources.reference: W. H. I. Bleek & L. C. Lloyd, Specimens of Bushman Folklore (1911)

attributes.name: serpent or tendril legs (anguipede form)
attributes.notes: Gold plaques and frontlets from kurgans such as Kul-Oba and Tovsta Mohyla (4th c. BCE) show the ancestress with coiling snake or vegetal tails in place of legs, often flanked by beasts as Potnia Theron (mistress of animals).

sources.reference: M. I. Artamonov, Treasures from Scythian Tombs (1969)

sacredAnimals.name: snakes
sacredAnimals.notes: Snakes form her very limbs and frame her image, marking her chthonic, generative character.

sources.reference: M. I. Artamonov, Treasures from Scythian Tombs (1969)

attributes.name: winged goddess flanked by beasts (Bosporan plaques)
attributes.notes: Among the Scythians she was aniconic, but on Graeco-Scythian goldwork from the Bosporus she appears as a winged mistress-of-animals, assimilated to a Potnia Theron / Aphrodite-Astarte type.

sources.reference: M. Ustinova, The Supreme Gods of the Bosporan Kingdom: Celestial Aphrodite and the Most High God (1999)

attributes.name: tall conical mask and stone-being body paint
attributes.notes: Impersonators wore a tall conical bark mask covering head and neck and a near-rectangular body frame; painted in patterns naming the four 'skies,' the men moved stiffly with clenched fists, feigning not to breathe because Shoort is made of stone.

sources.reference: Anne Chapman, Drama and Power in a Hunting Society: The Selk'nam of Tierra del Fuego (1982)

attributes.name: the sun
attributes.notes: The howenh Kran (Kren) was transformed into the sun; husband of the Moon-woman, he anchors the celestial pair of the Hain origin myth.

sources.reference: Martin Gusinde, Die Feuerland-Indianer, Band I: Die Selk'nam (1931)

attributes.name: the moon, its face marked by the men's revolt
attributes.notes: The howenh Kreeh (Kra) became the moon; the dark marks on her face are read as the scars from the men's overthrow of the women's rule that she once led.

sources.reference: Anne Chapman, Drama and Power in a Hunting Society: The Selk'nam of Tierra del Fuego (1982)
